title: Mixed-Precision Quantization for Deep Vision Models with Integer Quadratic Programming
problem: Uniform bit-width quantization causes significant accuracy degradation at low precision and inefficiency at high precision; existing mixed-precision methods assume independence of layer quantization errors, leading to suboptimal assignments.
motivation: Mixed-precision quantization is essential to balance accuracy and efficiency tradeoffs across layers, but cross-layer error dependencies have been ignored, leaving performance on the table.
method: CLADO approximates pairwise cross-layer quantization errors using linear equations learned on a small data subset, then assigns layer-wise bit-widths via Integer Quadratic Programming that explicitly models these dependencies to optimize the accuracy-efficiency frontier.
key_novelty: Capturing and optimizing cross-layer dependencies in quantization error rather than assuming layer independence.
contributions: Novel sensitivity-based MPQ formulation capturing pairwise cross-layer quantization error dependencies
Integer Quadratic Program solver for practical mixed-precision bit-width assignment
State-of-the-art results on ImageNet for CNN and vision transformer quantization
limitations: Not discussed; evaluation primarily on image classification tasks.
primary_theme: Cross-layer aware mixed-precision quantization via Integer QP
